source.authors: Piniak WED, Mann DA, Harms CA, Jones TT, Eckert SA
source.title: Hearing in the Juvenile Green Sea Turtle (Chelonia mydas): A Comparison of Underwater and Aerial Hearing Using Auditory Evoked Potentials

method: auditory evoked potentials (AEP) to underwater tone stimuli, sound pressure thresholds
conditions: Underwater. Five juvenile green turtles, all tested underwater and in air; the Methods print a mean of 34 kg (26 to 38 kg) and 65 cm curved carapace length; underwater AEPs were also taken on two turtles under anesthesia (one turtle with and without); thresholds are sound pressure, and the authors say background noise likely masked low-frequency stimuli so low-frequency thresholds are conservative; no inferential statistics were possible on the anesthesia comparison; tone frequencies presented were 50, 100, 200, 300, 400, 600, 800, 1600 and 3200 Hz, so the 50 Hz lower edge is the lowest frequency tested and the true lower limit is unknown; stimuli were attenuated from the highest level the system could generate at each frequency, and the range edges are reached by only some of the five turtles (Tables 1 and 2)
quote: Juvenile green turtles responded to signals between 50 and 1,600 Hz in water, with maximum sensitivity between 200 and 400 Hz (Table 1, Fig 4); sensitivity decreased sharply above 400 Hz.
note: Licence: Crossref (read through WebFetch) lists CC0 1.0 (creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/) for the version of record; the PMC copy read states the same. Range is the span of frequencies with an AEP response; best sensitivity 200 to 400 Hz; lowest pressure threshold 85 dB re 1 uPa-rms at 300 Hz (turtle L2). The paper also reports intensity-converted thresholds 2 to 39 dB lower underwater, mostly below 400 Hz, so the air-versus-water ranking depends on whether pressure or intensity is compared. The Abstract gives aerial maximum sensitivity as 300 to 400 Hz while the Results sentence gives 400 Hz. The authors assume sea turtles respond to acoustic pressure rather than intensity or particle motion. Species name Chelonia mydas (Linnaeus, 1758) is the GBIF accepted name. A different review-based hearing record for this species is on main (10.3354/esr00097), and a second review (10.3406/bavf.2021.70961); this is the primary study.

source.authors: Cobo-Cuan A, Feng AS, Zhang F, Narins PM
source.title: DPOAEs and tympanal membrane vibrations reveal adaptations of the sexually dimorphic ear of the concave-eared torrent frog, Odorrana tormota

method: distortion product otoacoustic emissions (DPOAE) DP-grams, range of f1 primary frequencies at which DP2f1–f2 exceeded noise + 2SD, f2/f1 = 1.1, L1 = L2 = 80 dB SPL
conditions: Wild adult frogs collected 3 to 17 April 2019 along Fu Creek, Huangshan, China; DPOAEs recorded within two days of capture under intramuscular pentobarbital anesthesia, from 10 non-gravid females and 10 males, primary tones L1 = L2 = 80 dB SPL for the DP-grams; DPOAEs are inner-ear emissions, not neural or behavioural thresholds, and the authors flag small samples for the tympanal-vibration (4 females, 4 males) and Eustachian-tube-closure (2 females, 4 males) parts
quote: In females, the DP2f1–f2 was distinguishable from system noise (≥ noise + 2SD) when f1 was between 2.27 and 6.73 kHz, except for one individual in which the DPOAE response extended to 8.36 kHz.
note: Licence: Crossref (read through WebFetch) lists CC BY 4.0 for the version of record, and the article text states it is licensed under CC BY 4.0. Quote reassembled from consecutive WebFetch segments and seen on two fetches. Female value. Best DPOAE sensitivity in the lower range 3.36 kHz (2.91 to 3.81 kHz, presumably the amphibian papilla) with a second peak near 5 kHz (my reading of the fetch; not quoted); female tympanum with Eustachian tubes open responded above 1 mm/s/Pa across 2 to 10 kHz with maximum at 3 kHz. One female responded to 8.36 kHz. The paper also gives the span of distortion-product frequencies (2 to 7.4 kHz), which is not a stimulus range. The paper says the species was formerly Amolops tormotus; GBIF accepts Odorrana tormota (Wu, 1977), Ranidae, Anura. The authors interpret each sex as most sensitive to the other sex's call frequencies; that is their interpretation. The DPOAE span shows where the inner ear responds under these stimulus levels and is not a behavioural hearing range.

method: distortion product otoacoustic emissions (DPOAE) DP-grams, range of f1 primary frequencies at which DP2f1–f2 exceeded noise + 2SD, f2/f1 = 1.1, L1 = L2 = 80 dB SPL
conditions: Wild adult frogs collected 3 to 17 April 2019 along Fu Creek, Huangshan, China; DPOAEs recorded within two days of capture under intramuscular pentobarbital anesthesia, from 10 non-gravid females and 10 males, primary tones L1 = L2 = 80 dB SPL for the DP-grams; DPOAEs are inner-ear emissions, not neural or behavioural thresholds, and the authors flag small samples for the tympanal-vibration (4 females, 4 males) and Eustachian-tube-closure (2 females, 4 males) parts
quote: In males, DP2f1–f2 was observed in a more extended frequency range, from 3.09 to 14.73 kHz.
note: Licence: Crossref (read through WebFetch) lists CC BY 4.0 for the version of record, and the article text states it is licensed under CC BY 4.0. Quote reassembled from consecutive WebFetch segments and seen on two fetches. Male value. Best DPOAE sensitivity at 5.05 kHz (3.64 to 7.55 kHz) and 7.64 kHz (6.36 to 10.45 kHz) in the low- and mid-frequency regions, and a third peak at 11.27 kHz (from the fetch summary; not quoted); two males responded up to the highest primary tested, 18.19 kHz. Males are small (mean 3.19 g against 16.72 g in females). GBIF accepts Odorrana tormota (Wu, 1977). Two males responded up to 18.19 kHz, the highest f1 used, so the upper edge is bounded by the stimulus set in those animals. The paper also gives the span of distortion-product frequencies (2.5 to 20 kHz; 20 kHz is a 2f2–f1 emission above every primary). The DPOAE span is not a behavioural hearing range.

eye: ear; peripheral auditory system via auditory brainstem response (ABR), not the eye

source.authors: Wang T, Li H, Chen B, Cui J, Shi H, Wang J
source.title: Effect of Temperature on the Plasticity of Peripheral Hearing Sensitivity to Airborne Sound in the Male Red-Eared Slider Trachemys scripta elegans

method: auditory brainstem response (ABR) to airborne tone bursts; hearing sensitivity bandwidth as defined by the authors
where: Results, Hearing Sensitivity Bandwidth and Auditory Brainstem Response Threshold
quote: The hearing sensitivity bandwidths were 0.2–0.5, 0.2–1.1, 0.2–1.3, and 0.2–1.5 kHz in the temperature groups of 10, 20, 30, and 40°C, respectively (Figure 2).
conditions: Body temperature group 10 C. Thirty-two 1-year-old male turtles bought from one farm in Hainan Province, deeply anesthetized with pentobarbital sodium for ABR; tone bursts (9 ms, 2 ms rise/fall) from 0.2 to 1.5 kHz in 100 Hz steps, so the lower edge of every range (0.2 kHz) and the 40 C upper edge (1.5 kHz) coincide with the limits of the stimulus set; groups of n = 7 (10 C), 7 (20 C), 6 (30 C) and 12 (40 C); airborne sound; males only; held 3 h at the test temperature before recording (cloacal temperature checked); the Discussion gives the stimulus level ceiling as 85 dB SPL, so a frequency falls outside the bandwidth when its threshold exceeds 85 dB SPL; the Methods do not define bandwidth (the Introduction: the range of frequency the auditory system could accept)
note: Licence: Crossref (read through WebFetch) lists CC BY 4.0 and the Frontiers PDF states the CC BY licence. Quote reassembled from two consecutive WebFetch segments. Temperature-group value (the sentence lists all four groups; the other three are filed as separate lines): lowest ABR threshold at 0.2 kHz (73.57 dB SPL). Thresholds fell from 10 to 30 C and the bandwidth kept widening at 40 C. Rank is subspecies; GBIF lists Trachemys scripta elegans (Wied, 1838) as accepted (usageKey 6157026). The Abstract itself does not list the bandwidths. Another turtle hearing record for this taxon on main is from a different paper (Christensen-Dalsgaard et al. 2012), which has no temperature series.
